title: Functor Hypergraph
semantics: Typed conceptual transport hypergraph. Each bridge retains its whole tail set (AND), hypotheses, conclusion map and evidence. Incidence edges are not independent implications.
certification_policy: No record is a Lean-certified functor. Promotion requires typed categories/object and morphism maps, identity/composition certificates, a current Lean gate, exact source fidelity and independent review. A span or analogy must never be relabeled automatically.

objects.label: Optimisation
objects.space: Finite-dimensional vector/Hilbert spaces; later explicit generalizations
objects.energy: Objective f, norm or Bregman geometry; minimizer or small optimality gap
objects.assumptions: Convexity, smoothness, strong convexity or PL are distinct hypotheses

objects.label: Riemannian Optimisation
objects.space: Smooth manifolds with specified metric, tangent spaces and retractions
objects.energy: Objective on a manifold; Riemannian gradient and stationarity
objects.assumptions: Geodesic convexity is not Euclidean convexity; curvature and retraction errors are explicit

objects.label: Sampling / MFLD
objects.space: Probability laws and Markov evolution on a state space
objects.energy: Gibbs/free-energy target; KL, Fisher information or Wasserstein error
objects.assumptions: Normalizability, regularity, ergodicity and LSI/PI conditions are separate from potential smoothness

objects.label: Statistical Optimal Transport
objects.space: Couplings, probability laws with finite moments, metric geometry
objects.energy: Transport cost, semidual, entropy regularization or barycenter objective
objects.assumptions: Absolute continuity, dual attainment, curvature and statistical identifiability are not automatic

objects.label: Lower bounds / SampleWiki
objects.space: Admissible algorithms, oracle transcripts and hard distributions
objects.energy: Information budget versus guaranteed error; not a new geometric state space
objects.assumptions: Specify oracle, adaptivity, randomness, starts, query cost and loss; reductions carry overhead

hyperedges.label: Change the metric, change the gradient
hyperedges.mechanism: A differential is a covector; a Riemannian metric converts it to a tangent gradient. Euclidean geometry is one instance.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Replace the ambient inner product by a metric. Distinguish pullback smoothness, geodesic convexity and a retraction-based local model.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: Descent and stationarity arguments transport only after bounding metric/retraction effects.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: A Euclidean Hessian lower bound in arbitrary coordinates does not imply geodesic strong convexity.

category_contract.objects: (space, metric, f, regularity) ↦ (manifold, metric, f, regularity).
category_contract.morphisms: A specified solution/certificate transport; no total morphism map is claimed.

hyperedges.label: One energy: minimizer or Gibbs law
hyperedges.mechanism: Optimization selects a minimum; an RGO draws from a normalized exponential of the same energy. This is a span through a common energy, not an equivalence of outputs.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Require existence (and, when claimed, uniqueness) of the minimizer; separately require 0 < partition function < infinity. Fix temperature and quadratic scaling.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: Quadratic regularization, convexity and some perturbation lemmas are shared; kernel simulation and target invariance are extra.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: An RGO is not itself the full proximal sampler, not automatically a JKO step, and not an exact deterministic proximal map.

hyperedges.label: Deterministic maps inside kernels
hyperedges.mechanism: Embed a measurable update map as a deterministic probability kernel. The product denotes first T, then S.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Updates must be measurable; pin kernel composition orientation and the measurable-space contracts.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: Transport deterministic iteration into a special case of Markov evolution; this does not manufacture Gibbs invariance.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: Continuity is not a substitute for checking the actual measurable structures. Stochastic kernels are not generally deterministic maps.

category_contract.morphisms: Measurable T ↦ the Dirac kernel K_T.
category_contract.identity: Target: K_id is the identity kernel; no local certificate yet.
category_contract.composition: Target: K_(S∘T) = K_T K_S with the stated convention; no local certificate yet.

hyperedges.label: Energy descent on probability laws
hyperedges.mechanism: A free energy on probability laws generates Fokker–Planck through the Wasserstein gradient-flow interpretation.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Fix Euclidean base, positive temperature, finite moments/entropy and weak solution or EDI/EVI hypotheses. Nonlinear first variations require additional contracts.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: Energy-dissipation proofs connect sampling evolution with optimization over measures.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: Formal Otto notation alone is not a proof of existence, uniqueness, SDE-law correspondence or EVI; W2 is not globally a classical smooth manifold.

hyperedges.label: MFLD: entropy sandwich and PL controls
hyperedges.mechanism: For a differentiable mixture-convex F, set L=F+λ Ent and q_μ proportional to exp(−δF(μ)/λ). Gibbs variational inequalities sandwich the gap.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Require a minimizer, normalizable q_μ, and the source differentiability/integrability contracts. Uniform LSI for q_μ is an EXTRA hypothesis, not a consequence of mixture convexity.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: LSI KL≤I/(2ρ) and dL/dt=−λ²I give a PL-type dissipation control. The lower sandwich is a KL-growth control; W2 quadratic growth additionally needs a transport-entropy inequality for μ*.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: Mixture convexity ≠ displacement convexity. Neither LSI nor W2 quadratic growth follows merely from an entropy term. This connects proof mechanisms, not identical geometries.

hyperedges.label: Convex duality to transport duality
hyperedges.mechanism: Coupling optimization and Kantorovich potentials reuse convex duality, with feasibility and topology specific to transport.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Retain the exact source hypotheses for no duality gap and attainment; noncompact spaces need extra care.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: Convex conjugacy and variational inequalities feed transport-map stability and entropic duals.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: Equality of optimal values does not by itself give optimizers, smooth potentials, a Monge map or statistical rates.

hyperedges.label: Taylor structure to sampling accuracy
hyperedges.mechanism: Borrow high-order remainder tools from optimization; close stochastic local error, stability and invariant-target obligations separately.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Keep p (potential regularity), q (oracle derivative access), k (dynamical order) and r (discretization accuracy) independent; specify operator norm and all constants.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: Target a cost-aware upper bound under a fixed oracle, then isolate which improvement really comes from additional smoothness.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: Better discretization can already occur under Lipschitz gradients; high-order dynamics does not automatically mean high-order derivative queries.

hyperedges.label: Reduction transports hardness, not analogy
hyperedges.mechanism: If an algorithm for B solves hard task A through a valid simulation, hardness of A lower-bounds cost for B with explicit overhead.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Prove preservation of the hard-instance class, permitted oracle answers, adaptivity/randomness and the error conversion ψ; state start and failure probabilities.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: Only a certified reduction allows an optimization or statistical lower bound to transfer to sampling.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: A common convexity lemma or similar rate exponent is not a reduction. Smoothness upper-bound lemmas are not prerequisites of a hard-instance proof.

hyperedges.label: OT estimation and sampling: distinct budgets
hyperedges.mechanism: OT statistical estimation controls uncertainty from observed samples; computational sampling controls the cost of generating approximate draws.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Record data access versus potential/gradient access, population class, dimension, metric and any reduction between experiments.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: Common discrepancy/testing lemmas may be reused while the two notions of sample complexity stay distinct.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: No minimax statistical rate becomes a sampling query lower bound without a source-backed, cost-preserving reduction.
